notices.text: NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING Supplemental Budget The Klickitat County Board of Commissioners will meet May 12th, 2026, at 1:30 pm. Please join the meeting at the Klickitat County Services Building in the Chambers of the Board of County Commissioners, or virtually via Zoom, meeting ID 586587651. They will hold a Public Hearing and consider amendments to the 2026 budget as summarized below. Information concerning these changes may be obtained at the Commissioners' Office, 115 W Court St. Rm 201, by calling 509.773.2331, or viewing this notice and supporting detail on the Klickitat County website at Board of County Commissioners Agenda page or the Fiscal Services department page. Written comment will be accepted via email to bocc@klickitatcounty.org or in the Commissioner’s office on or before May 12th, 2026 at 1:30pm, with the subject line: 2026-1 BUDGET AMENDMENT. Board of County Commissioners, Ron Ihrig, Chairman Fund, Expense Request 001 General - 207,920.00 111 Elections - 80,000.00 124 Investigations - 73,860.00 125 Cumulative Reserve - 567,238.00 133 Affordable Housing - 50,000.00 139 Landfill Gas Improvements - 250,000.00 TOTAL - 1,229,018.00 NOTICE OF PUBLIC COMMENT PERIOD COLUMBIA GORGE ALUMINUM PROSPECTIVE PURCHASER CONSENT DECREE, REMEDIAL INVESTIGATION/FEASIBILITY STUDY, AND CLEANUP ACTION PLAN The Dept of Ecology (Ecology) invites you to comment on the proposed Prospective Purchaser Consent Decree (PPCD), Remedial Investigation and Feasibility Study (RI/FS), and Cleanup Action Plan (CAP) for the former Columbia Gorge Aluminum site. The comment period runs 12:01 a.m., April 30 through 11:59 p.m., June 16, 2026. Read or get a copy of the proposed actions and supporting documents at the following locations: Department of Ecology, 300 Desmond Drive SE, Lacey, WA, (360) 407-7393; Goldendale Community Library, 1131 West Burgen Street, Goldendale; online at https://bit.ly/ecology11797 , and in-person by appointment 360-280-4328 at the Ecology Lacey Office, 300 Desmond Drive SE, Lacey. Written comments may be submitted online at https://bit.ly/4swqHxp or by mail to Dave Johnson, Department of Ecology, Industrial Section, P.O. Box 47600, Olympia, WA 98504-7600. Attend the virtual public meeting and hearing on ZOOM, June 3, 2026, at 6 p.m. to see a presentation about the cleanup process and the documents available for public comment, ask questions, and offer oral comments about the cleanup documents. Please register for this meeting and hearing at https://bit.ly/Ecology11797meeting Registration is required. Ecology invites you to comment on the following draft cleanup documents: · Cleanup Action Plan (CAP): The proposed plan outlines the cleanup actions required by Ecology in order to remove contaminants to meet health and environmental standards. The final CAP will become an enforceable component of the PPCD (exhibit D of the PPCD). · Legal agreement: Ecology plans to enter into a Prospective Purchaser Consent Decree (PPCD) with FFP Project 101 LLC that requires it to clean up a portion of the former Columbia Gorge Aluminum Site. · Remedial Investigation and Feasibility Study (RI/FS): The remedial investigation outlines testing plans that identify the contamination at the site and its extent. The Feasibility Study evaluates the options for dealing with that contamination. The cleanup documents propose excavating a formerly closed waste landfill (West Surface Impoundment-WSI) and contaminated soil related to the former aluminum smelter. The Columbia Gorge Aluminum smelter operated under various owners until it closed in 2003. Starting in 1980, owners managed hazardous and solid waste at several locations on the site. The facility was added to the Hazardous Sites list in 1990. Industrial practices and historical land use by the smelter owners and operators have resulted in contamination at the site. The investigation, identification of cleanup methods, and cleanup plan for the site, seek to address this contamination to redevelop the property. Ecology issued the final State Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) for the Goldendale Energy Storage Project on December 21, 2022 and the Clean Water Act 401 Water Quality Certification on May 22, 2023. The EIS summarizes findings from the State Environmental Policy Act (SEPA) analysis of potential project impacts (including cleanup work). The EIS also describes the steps that can be taken to minimize project impacts. These findings were considered when we developed the draft cleanup action plan. When the comment period ends, we will review all comments received before we make a final decision on the documents. If you would like to be added to the list of interested parties for the cleanup at Columbia Gorge Aluminum and receive updates on Ecology’s Industrial Section actions at the site, contact Tara Roberts at 360-280-4325 or tara.roberts@ecy.wa.gov . To request an ADA accommodation, email tara.roberts@ecy.wa.gov , call 360-280-4325, or dial 711 to call through the Washington Telecommunications Relay for services like text telephone (TTY). Visit Ecology.wa.gov/ADA for more accessibility information.

EFSEC and the Applicant have agreed an environmental impact statement (EIS) under RCW 43.21C.030(2)(c) will be prepared. Not all elements of the environment outlined in the SEPA rules (WAC 197-11-444) are expected to be required in the study. An environmental checklist, the application, studies, and plans prepared by the applicant (appendices), and other materials related to environmental impacts are available on the Project website: https://efsec.wa.gov/facilities/cascade-renewable-transmission and at libraries: Washington State Library Fort Vancouver Regional Libraries (Stevenson Community Library, North Bonneville Library, White Salmon Valley Library, Goldendale Community Library, Vancouver Community Library) Public Comment Period: Comments will be accepted from May 1, through June 1, 2026. notices.text: Legal Notice for Request for Proposals (RFP) Senior Nutrition - Congregate and Home Delivered Nutrition Services in Southwest Washington The Area Agency on Aging and Disabilities of Southwest Washington (AAADSW) is designated by the State of Washington as the Area Agency on Aging to serve Clark, Cowlitz, Wahkiakum, Klickitat and Skamania Counties. As the area agency on aging, AAADSW plans, advocates for, develops, coordinates and supports a comprehensive service delivery system in the region for persons who are 60 years of age or older, persons with disabilities who are 18 years of age or older, and caregivers of aging and/or disabled persons. These programs are among the services overseen by AAADSW (see our website at www.HelpingElders.org). RFP Announcements: AAADSW will contract with one or more successful bidders to provide Congregate Nutrition Services and/or Home Delivered Nutrition Services in one or more counties in AAADSW’s five county service area. The Senior Nutrition Program, funded in part by the Older Americans Act, provides Congregate and Home Delivered meals to adults aged 60 and older and to other eligible individuals. These meals are provided in a variety of settings such as senior and community centers, churches, and individual residences; and must contain at least one-third of the U.S. daily recommended dietary allowances. Service providers must also ensure access to a range of additional services such as nutrition screening, assessment, education, and outreach and referral. Applicants may choose to apply for one or both services under this RFP, and will be contracted for consecutive one year contracts for service up to four total years- from January 1, 2027 through December 31, 2030. Eligibility: Eligible applicants must be a verifiable legal public or private entity, hold a valid Washington State Business License, and have three (3) years of experience for the services to be provided. Applicants must also comply with all applicable local, state, and federal laws, and AAADSW policies. Organizations that have been debarred, suspended, proposed for debarment, declared ineligible or excluded from participating in a contract by any Federal or Washington State agency will not be considered. Fiscal and management references will be requested. Providers may be required to show demonstrated experience and capability to provide all aspects of senior nutrition services such as food services management, targeted outreach, facility and equipment management, program and human resource management, fundraising, volunteer development, and community nutrition education. Applicants must demonstrate sufficient working capital and fiscal administrative capability. Mandatory requirements to apply (RFP Packets): Entities interested must request an RFP packet, which details the application process and criteria. To receive the mandatory RFP packet, please send a request to: AAADSWcontracts@dshs.wa.gov Deadlines: Interested entities must request the mandatory RFP packet(s) and submit to AAADSW the Notice of Intent to Propose form(s) therein before 5:00 pm Pacific Time on Friday July 31, 2026. Submissions received after this deadline will not be considered. AAADSW is an Equal Opportunity Agency Women-owned, Minority-owned and Veteran-owned businesses are encouraged to apply

notices.text: NOTICE OF ELECTION Notice is hereby given that a Primary will be held in Klickitat County, Washington, August 4, 2026, in all precincts within Klickitat County. The election will be conducted by mail ballot. Voter registration forms are available at post offices, libraries, or at the Auditor’s Office. Registrations and updates may also be submitted online at votewa.gov . The last day to register to vote, transfer or update an existing registration by mail or online is July 27, 2026. The last day to register to vote or update your voter registration in person is August 4, 2026 in the Klickitat County Auditor’s Office, 205 S. Columbus Ave. Room 203. On or before July 17, 2026, the Auditor’s Office will mail, or cause to be mailed, to each qualified voter within the county, a ballot. Ballots returned by mail must be postmarked by August 4, 2026. No postage is required if mailed within the United States. Ballots returned in-person to our office or dropped into a designated drop box must be returned by 8:00 P.M. on August 4, 2026. Replacement ballots may be obtained from the Auditor’s Office or by visiting votewa.gov . The Auditor’s Office shall provide the availability of registration and voting aids, assistance to elderly and disabled persons, and procedures for voting by mail. Contact the Auditor’s Office if you need assistance with a mail ballot. The Accessible Voting Unit is equipped with audio and visual technology which allows voters with limited vision, hearing, or physical disabilities to vote more independently. This unit is available in the Auditor’s Office beginning July 17, 2026, through August 3, 2026, during regular business hours Monday through Friday from 8:30 A.M. to noon. and 1:00 P.M.to 5:00 P.M. On Election Day, August 4, 2026, the Accessible Voting Unit is available from 8:30 A.M. to 8:00 P.M. After review of the completed environmental checklist and other information on file the Klickitat County Responsible Official has determined that this proposal will not have probable significant adverse impacts on the environment. notices.text: PUBLIC NOTICE Cupertino Electric inc, 1132 North Seventh St., San Jose California 95112-4427 is seeking coverage under the Washington State Department of Ecology’s Construction Stormwater NPDES and State Waste Discharge General Permit. The proposed project Bluebird Solar LLC is Located at the intersection of Big Horn Rd. and Van Nostern Rd. in Bickleton WA in Klickitat County. This project involves 724 acres of soil disturbance for industrial construction activities. The receiving water is Wood Creek. Any persons desiring to present their views to the Department of Ecology regarding this application may do so in writing within thirty days of the last date of publication of this notice. Comments shall be submitted to the Department of Ecology. Any person interested in the department’s action on this application may notify the department of their interest within the thirty days of the last date of publication of this notice. Ecology reviews public comments and considers whether discharges from this project would cause a measurable change in receiving water quality, and, if so, whether the project is necessary and in the overriding public interest according to Tier II antidegradation requirements under WAC 173-201A-320. Comments can be submitted to: Department of Ecology Attn: Water Quality Program, Construction Stormwater PO Box 47696, Olympia, WA 98504-7696 Email: ecyrewqianoi@ecy.wa.gov

notices.text: NOTICE OF ELECTION Notice is hereby given that a General Election will be held in Klickitat County, Washington, November 3, 2026, in all precincts within Klickitat County. The election will be conducted by mail ballot. Voter registration forms are available at post offices, libraries, or at the Auditor’s Office. Registrations and updates may also be submitted online at votewa.gov . The last day to register to vote, transfer or update an existing registration by mail or online is October 26, 2026. The last day to register to vote or update your voter registration in person is November 3, 2026 in the Klickitat County Auditor’s Office, 205 S. Columbus Ave. Room 203. On or before October 14, 2026, the Auditor’s Office will mail, or cause to be mailed, to each qualified voter within the county, a ballot. Ballots returned by mail must be postmarked by November 3, 2026. No postage is required if mailed within the United States. Ballots returned in-person to our office or dropped into a designated drop box must be returned by 8:00 P.M. on November 3, 2026. Replacement ballots may be obtained from the Auditor’s Office or by visiting votewa.gov . The Auditor’s Office shall provide the availability of registration and voting aids, assistance to elderly and disabled persons, and procedures for voting by mail. Contact the Auditor’s Office if you need assistance with a mail ballot. The Accessible Voting Unit is equipped with audio and visual technology which allows voters with limited vision, hearing, or physical disabilities to vote more independently. This unit is available in the Auditor’s Office beginning October 16, 2026, through November 2, 2026, during regular business hours Monday through Friday from 8:30 A.M. to noon. and 1:00 P.M.to 5:00 P.M. On Election Day, November 3, 2026, the Accessible Voting Unit is available from 8:30 A.M. to 8:00 P.M. If you need an accessibility accommodation, please contact the Auditor’s Office at (509) 773-4001 or by emailing voting@klickitatcounty.gov , no later than five working days prior to the date service is needed. Pursuant to RCW 29A.60, the canvassing board will hold a public meeting at 8:30 A.M., on November 17, 2026, to examine returns and at 8:30 A.M., on November 24, 2026, to certify the cumulative results, precinct results and a reconciliation report of the votes cast. These meetings will be held in the Klickitat County Services Building located at 115 W. Court St., Goldendale, WA 98620 in the Mt. St. Helens Conference Room on the third floor. For google meets login information, visit our website at: http://www.klickitatcounty.gov/1136/ElectionsVoter-Registration and select the Current Election tab. Additional information may be obtained by phone (509) 773-4001 and by visiting www.klickitatcounty.gov/1136/ElectionsVoter-Registration . Dated this 7th day of October, 2026. Heather Jobe, Klickitat County Auditor and Ex Officio Supervisor of Elections

notices.text: PUBLIC NOTICE The following measures will be submitted to voters on the November 3, 2026 General Election ballot: INITIATIVE TO THE PEOPLE IP26-645 - Initiative Measure No. IP26-645 concerns state and local taxes. This measure would repeal a 9.9% tax on annual individual income over $1,000,000; prohibit taxes measured by individual income and taxes on individual income or the receipt of individual income; and define “income.” This measure would decrease funding for public K-12 education, higher education (including universities and community colleges), and human services (primarily healthcare). INITIATIVES TO THE LEGISLATURE IL26-001 - Initiative Measure No. IL26-001 concerns parental rights relating to their children in public school. This measure would repeal amendments to a statute listing certain rights of parents and guardians of public-school children and re-enact the law as it was originally enacted by Initiative to the Legislature 2081. IL26-638 - Initiative Measure No. IL26-638 concerns participation in athletics at K-12 schools. This measure would prohibit students it defines as “biologically male” from competing in certain school athletic activities intended for female students only. It would require verification of biological sex by students’ healthcare providers

notices.text: RFQ for ON-CALL ENGINEERING SERVICES CITY OF STEVENSON The City of Stevenson is requesting statements of qualification from qualified consulting engineering firms to provide on-call professional engineering services. Services may include public works planning and design, development review, construction management, grant funding assistance, and other engineering services related to the City’s infrastructure and operations. The selected consultant(s) will provide technical assistance, consultation, and professional engineering support to the Public Works Department, City staff, officials, and developers on an as-needed basis. The City anticipates selecting one or more firms to provide services under a multi-year on-call professional services agreement. Submittals are due by 3:00 PM on Thursday, November 19th at Stevenson City Hall. Interested firms must complete a statement of qualifications package that can be requested from the City or found on the City website. The City will be considering qualifications of key personnel, relevant experience, and previous performance on similar projects and if the firm has Washington State Certification as Minority Enterprise Participation. The City of Stevenson is an equal opportunity and affirmative action employer. Minority- and women-owned firms are encouraged to submit proposals.
